findings.evidence: PolynomialSigns.lean:23 `variable ... [IsRealClosed R]`; the proof body uses only `natDegree_le_two_of_irreducible` and `TauCeti.irreducible_quadratic_eval_*` (lines 38,54-57), i.e. real-closedness is a proof convenience; SturmInfinity.lean:67-93 uses only `signs_top`/`signs_bot` plus `List.signVariations_congr`.
findings.fix: Drop `[IsRealClosed R]` from the `variable` line (PolynomialSigns.lean:23) and prove by a Cauchy-type bound: for `p ≠ 0` take `B = 1 + (∑ i ∈ range p.natDegree, |p.coeff i|) / |p.leadingCoeff|`, so `|leadingCoeff * x^n| > |∑_{i<n} coeff i * x^i|` for `x > B`. Then restate `signs_top`/`signs_bot`/`exists_top`/`exists_bot` over `[Field R] [LinearOrder R] [IsStrictOrderedRing R]`.
findings.issue: `sign_at_top` (line 26) and `sign_at_bot` (line 63) assume `[IsRealClosed R]`, but both hold over any ordered field; real-closedness is only used by the chosen linear/quadratic factorization proof. The restriction propagates to `signs_top`, `signs_bot`, `exists_top`, `exists_bot` (SturmInfinity.lean:40,52,67,81), none of which use IVT, so the entire signs-at-infinity layer is unusable over e.g. ℚ.

findings.evidence: SturmSum.lean:94 applies `hsimple r hr` inside the `hjump` callback, where `sum_jumps` only invokes `hjump` at `r ∈ S` with `a < r < b` (Jumps.lean:73-76, `r := T.min'` of `S.filter (a < · ∧ · < b)`); SturmTarski.lean:150 and 178 apply it at `r` drawn from `p.roots.toFinset.filter (fun r => a < r ∧ r < b)`; SturmTarski.lean:205 applies it as `hsimple r (hZ r hr)` for `r ∈ Z` only.
findings.fix: Weaken to `(hsimple : ∀ r, a < r → r < b → p.eval r = 0 → p.derivative.eval r ≠ 0)` in `Regular.sum_of_regular_endpoints`, `Regular.sum`, `tarski`, and the half-line/`sturmSeq` corollaries; enable it by restricting `Finset.sum_jumps` (Jumps.lean:57) so `hconst`/`hjump` are only required for subintervals, i.e. add `a₀ ≤ a` and `b ≤ b₀` to the callback hypotheses and carry them through the strong induction. In `tarski_zero` use `(hsimple : ∀ r ∈ Z, p.derivative.eval r ≠ 0)` — a one-line change.
findings.issue: Interval theorems assume the head has simple roots everywhere in `R` although only roots in `(a, b)` are ever used: `Regular.sum_of_regular_endpoints` (line 73), `Regular.sum` (line 127), `tarski` (SturmTarski.lean:96), `tarski_sturmSeq` (SturmTarski.lean:214), `root_count` (SturmTarski.lean:233), `tarski_Ioi`/`tarski_Iio` (SturmInfinity.lean:99,123, where only `(a,∞)`/`(-∞,b)` matters). Consequently the theorem cannot be applied on an interval to a polynomial whose multiple roots lie outside it — the standard subdivision use case. `tarski_zero` (SturmTarski.lean:199) has the same defect: it needs `hsimple` only at elements of `Z`.

findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/Data/List/SignVariations.lean:56 `signVariations_singleton (a : α) : signVariations [a] = 0`; the three proofs are `simpa [variation_eq, variationTop/variationBot] using hz` from `tarski_zero` (SturmInfinity.lean:172,183,194); grep for `tarski_zero_` finds no other use in TauCeti/.
findings.fix: State the actual content once — `theorem tarski_zero (hseed : TarskiSeed p f 0) (hsimple : ∀ r ∈ Z, p.derivative.eval r ≠ 0) (hZ : ∀ r ∈ Z, p.eval r = 0) : ∑ r ∈ Z, (SignType.sign (f.eval r) : ℤ) = 0` — and delete the three variants (or replace them with the concrete `sturmSeq` half-line corollaries that would actually need them).
findings.issue: `tarski_zero_Ioi` (165), `tarski_zero_Iio` (176), `tarski_zero_univ` (187) are three instantiations of `tarski_zero` whose left-hand side is identically `0`: `variation [p] x = List.signVariations [p.eval x] = 0`, and likewise `variationTop [p] = variationBot [p] = 0`. They have no in-repo caller and add no content over `tarski_zero`, which itself carries decorative `{a b : R}` for a `0 - 0` left side.

summary: The sign-at-infinity lemmas are confined to real closed fields although they hold over any ordered field, the interval Sturm–Tarski theorems assume simple roots globally although only roots inside the interval are used, and the `tarski_zero` family states a difference that is identically zero and is instantiated three more times with no caller.
